strings.name: Abdul Samad Rabiu
strings.role: Founder and executive chairman of BUA Group
strings.summary: Rabiu is a Nigerian entrepreneur who founded BUA in 1988 and expanded from commodity trading into food processing and cement manufacturing. He chairs BUA Foods and BUA Cement and supports education, health and social development through ASR Africa.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026; the latest project report was published November 5. Distinguishes the group from listed subsidiaries, listing from merger, and pledges from delivered projects; representation is not personal attendance.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed BUA Group’s cement and food industries, contributing to Nigerian basic manufacturing and regional supply.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Studied economics at Capital University in Ohio, USA, then returned to Nigeria to join the family business.
strings.facts.f2.label: Distinct roles
strings.facts.f2.value: Chairs BUA Cement; its managing director and chief executive officer is Yusuf Haliru Binji.
strings.highlights.h1.title: From trading to manufacturing
strings.highlights.h1.text: Developed food and cement businesses through acquisitions and industrial investment; the two businesses separately entered Nigeria’s capital market.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Establishing ASR Africa
strings.highlights.h2.text: Focuses on education, health and social development; the annual US$100 million was a funding commitment at launch, not audited annual spending.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Foundation hands over university administrative building
strings.timeline.t1.text: ASR Africa reports handing over a building valued at NGN250 million to the College of Health Sciences at Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto; Ubon Udoh represented him.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Speaks at Nigerian Economic Summit
strings.timeline.t2.text: Reports record his keynote at the 32nd summit in Abuja, calling for shared participation in national development.
strings.timeline.t3.title: BUA Foods lists
strings.timeline.t3.text: Lists by introduction on the Nigerian Exchange as BUAFOODS, without an additional public sale of shares.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Launches ASR Africa
strings.timeline.t4.text: Announces US$100 million annually, divided equally between Nigeria and the rest of Africa, for education, health and social development.
strings.timeline.t5.title: BUA Cement lists
strings.timeline.t5.text: Following the merger of CCNN and Obu Cement, BUA Cement lists on the Nigerian Stock Exchange.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Acquires control of CCNN
strings.timeline.t6.text: BUA acquires a controlling stake in Cement Company of Northern Nigeria, expanding cement manufacturing.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Acquires Nigerian Oil Mills
strings.timeline.t7.text: BUA acquires the edible-oil processor, supporting its expansion from trading into manufacturing.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founds BUA
strings.timeline.t8.text: Establishes a commodity-trading business, later expanding into industrial manufacturing and infrastructure investment.
